title: Split the Power
story:
The reactor gives out power in whole units. Every module gets the same amount, and whatever can't be split evenly goes to the spare battery.

Input: two whole numbers `P` (power units, 0–1000000) and `N` (modules, 1–1000).

Output, two lines:
`Each: Q`, the units each module gets
`Spare: S`, the units left over

Example: `17 5` prints `Each: 3` then `Spare: 2`.
hints: Dividing two ints already throws away the fraction. Here that's exactly what you want.
The leftover is the remainder: the `%` operator.
`printf("Each: %d\n", power / modules);` and the same shape with `%` for Spare.
